title: Kornati with Toddlers & Young Kids: Family Guide 2027
metaDescription: Kornati with toddlers: boat tours from Murter and Zadar, child prices in €, swim stops, sandy beaches, park fees and where to stay with young children.
content:
## Is Kornati Suitable for Toddlers and Young Children?

Yes, as a day trip. Kornati National Park covers 89 islands, islets and rocks across 216.78 km². It has no villages, no shops and almost no paved ground. Accommodation is limited to a few basic fishermen's cottages and konobas on Kornat island that are mainly used by sailors. Families with children under 6 get the best result by staying on the mainland side or on Murter island and visiting for one day.

The main limits for toddlers are time on the boat, sun exposure and the lack of facilities. The sights are cliffs, bays and viewpoints, not playgrounds. Children aged 3–8 usually enjoy the swim stops and boat deck. Under 2, the day depends on naps, shade and snacks.

## Best Base for Families: Murter, Jezera or Betina

Murter island is the closest gateway. The Murter main port is about 20 km from the park entrance at Opat, so boats reach the first islands within an hour or so. Jezera and Betina are quieter villages on the same island with pebble and concrete swimming spots, shallow water and short walking distances.

Vodice and Biograd are larger alternatives with more shops, pharmacies and restaurants. Zadar works if the family wants city sights as well, but the boat ride from Zadar to the park is about 2.5 hours each way on at least one operator. That is long for a toddler.

**Opinion:** Skip the fast speedboat tours for children under 4. They cost €150 or more per adult, are loud, bounce on waves and have little shade. A slow, large excursion boat from Murter with a covered saloon and toilets is the better choice. It costs less than half as much.

## Boat Tours from Murter: Times, Prices and Child Rates

Most full-day tours leave the Murter main port at 09:00 and return between 17:30 and 18:00. Typical program: a cruise past the outer cliffs, a stop on Mana island with a short walk to a viewpoint, lunch on board, and a swim stop at Lojena bay on Levrnaka island. Lojena is the best-known beach stop and has a sandy-pebble shore, which is easier for small children than bare rock.

- **Re di Mare:** €60–65 adults, €30–35 for ages 5–12, free for ages 0–4. Large modern boat for up to 150 people.
- **Visko from Jezera:** €35 adults, €18 for ages 5–12, free for ages 0–5. Small fishing boat for 30–50 people, one swim stop.
- **Torcida:** wooden sailboat for 40–55 people, adults €65, ages 5–12 €35.

The national park ticket, lunch and a welcome drink are included on most of these. Child discounts and free-age limits differ between boats (under 3, under 4 and under 5 all exist), so check the exact cut-off when booking if the child is close to the limit.

## Tours from Zadar and Vodice

Zadar tours usually leave at 07:30–08:00 and often combine Kornati with Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi Otok. One operator charges €65 for adults, €32.50 for ages 5–12, €13 for ages 3–4 and nothing for children under 3. Others list adult prices of €56–70. A day on the boat lasts 9–10 hours, with roughly 5 hours spent in transit, so it works best for children who nap on moving boats.

Vodice and Murter are the shortest transfers. Vodice-based tours cost around €79 per adult on the main operator listed.

## Private Boat or Charter with Young Children

A family on a rented or chartered boat pays the park fee per boat, not per person. A boat up to 6.99 m pays €25 in low season (January–May and October–December) and €45 in high season (June–September) when bought online in advance. A boat of 7–10.99 m pays €30 and €65. Buying from the ranger boat inside the park costs about double, so buy before sailing, via the park webshop or the mySea portal.

A private skipper gives control over timing: short hops, nap breaks and anchoring in calm bays. Check that life jackets in the correct child size are on board. They are not always provided.

## When to Go

June to September is the swimming window, with sea temperatures of 20–27°C. June and September have far fewer boats than July and August and similar water clarity. For toddlers, late June and early-to-mid September avoid the hottest midday temperatures. Mid-October boats still run on some routes, but the water is cooler and shade matters less than wind protection.

## What to Pack for Toddlers

- UV swimsuit and wide-brim hat. There is almost no natural shade on the islands.
- Water shoes. Most shores are sharp limestone.
- Snacks, water and a spare change of clothes. Lunch on board is a fixed grilled fish or meat menu, so ask in advance for a vegetarian or child portion.
- Seasickness remedies approved for the child's age, and a lightweight carrier instead of a stroller, because stroller access is poor.
- Cash for small purchases. Konobas and kiosks on the islands may not take cards.

## Local Tips for Families

- Choose a boat with a covered saloon and a toilet. Smaller fishing boats are charming but often have a basic toilet and open decks.
- Sit near the middle of the boat to reduce rocking, and avoid the front.
- Book an afternoon nap time into the plan: the longest crossing usually happens after lunch.
- Swimming is banned in the four strict-protection zones, so do not choose an unguided swim stop in an unknown bay. The tour boat captains know which bays are open.
- Sandy-beach alternatives: Sakarun beach on Dugi Otok is a classic family stop on some Zadar speedboat itineraries. Lojena on Levrnaka is the easy-access option on Murter tours.

## Safety Notes

There is no hospital in the park. The nearest medical services are in Murter, Vodice and Šibenik, and the nearest hospital is in Šibenik. Mobile reception is patchy among the outer islands. Tell the crew about any allergies before lunch is served. Children should wear life jackets on deck when the boat is moving, especially on smaller vessels.

faq.question: Can you bring a toddler to Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: Yes. Boat operators accept infants and toddlers, and many do not charge for children under 3 to 5 years, depending on the operator. Plan for 9–10 hours away from the mainland with limited shade, so bring sun protection, snacks and a carrier.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati boat trip cost for a family?
faq.answer: From Murter, a full-day tour costs about €60–65 for adults and €30–35 for ages 5–12, with younger children free on many boats. A family of two adults and a 6-year-old pays roughly €150–165 on the larger boats. A cheaper fishing-boat tour from Jezera costs about €35 per adult and €18 per child.

faq.question: Where should families stay for Kornati?
faq.answer: Murter, Jezera and Betina on Murter island are the closest bases, with Vodice and Biograd as larger alternatives. The park itself has almost no accommodation. Staying on Murter keeps the boat trip to about 9 hours door to door.

faq.question: Are there sandy beaches in Kornati for small children?
faq.answer: Lojena bay on Levrnaka island is the standard swim stop on Murter tours and is easier for children than bare rock. Sakarun beach on Dugi Otok is sandy and appears on some Zadar itineraries. Most other shores are limestone, so water shoes help.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Kornati with children?
faq.answer: June and September are the best months. The sea is 20–27°C and boats are fewer than in July and August. Avoid midday heat on open decks.

faq.question: Do I need to buy a park ticket for children?
faq.answer: On organized tours the ticket is included in the price. On a private boat the park charges per boat, not per person, with €25 low season and €45 high season for boats up to 6.99 m when bought in advance.

quickAnswer: Kornati suits toddlers as a day trip, not an overnight base. Take a 9-hour boat tour from Murter (about €60–65 adults, free under 5 on some boats) and sleep in Murter, Jezera or Betina. Pack sun cover, snacks and a car seat alternative, and choose a slow, shaded boat.
